title: Suspect arrested, charged with arson at Orthodox church in Canada
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) — A man was arrested and charged with arson in connection with a recent fire that destroyed a 68-year-old Orthodox church filled with priceless artwork and icons in a small Canadian town. A Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) detachment for Meadow Lake, Saskatchewan, said in a statement that 28-year-old Gavin Burnouf was arrested on November 2 and charged with one count of arson under Section 434 of Canada’s Criminal Code. The charge was in connection with a fire at All Saints Orthodox Church in Meadow Lake. … In 2021 alone, there were 91 cases of arson, the same year that the mainstream media ran with inflammatory and dubious claims that hundreds of children were buried and disregarded by Catholic priests and nuns who ran some Canadian residential schools. The reality is that, after four years, there have been no mass graves discovered at residential schools. However, amid the spread of the baseless claims, more than 100 churches, most of them Catholic and many of them on indigenous lands that serve the local population, have been burned to the ground, vandalized , or desecrated in Canada since the spring of 2021.

title: Jim Caviezel calls out Leo XIV: ‘Good men need to start fighting’
description: Bringing you the news from a traditional Catholic perspective. ( LifeSiteNews ) — Catholic actor Jim Caviezel, famous for playing Jesus Christ in The Passion of the Christ , called out popes, prelates, and clergymen for offering only a watered-down version of the Gospel because they are “afraid.” … “They like to play pattycake in church,” as if “everything is fine,” he added. “We’re in a time of war, and good men need to stand up and start fighting.” Caviezel, 58, has long been known for being an outspoken promoter of the Catholic faith. He made his remarks while promoting his new film, Ghost Soldier , which will be released in theaters on Veterans’ Day, November 11.

title: Trump says he refuses to forgive his enemies even if it keeps him from heaven
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) — During an extraordinary 60 Minutes interview , President Donald Trump repeatedly suggested that he is unwilling to forgive his enemies, even if that meant being barred from entering heaven. Catholic correspondent Ross Douthat pointedly asked the president, “What do you think will happen to you when you die? Do you think you’re going to heaven?” … “Come on! Help me out here!” exclaimed Douthat, giving Trump another opportunity to rethink and recant. “I probably cannot do that, no, because I do hate some of my enemies and I always will,” he declared. “Lots of presidents are remembered with a single line: ‘He freed the slaves.’ ‘He won the Cold War,’” noted Douthat. “A hundred years from now, while you’re working out your situation in purgatory, what is the line that your presidency is remembered with?”
